description: In response to err-20261024T164928-M4FT4E (generated PDFs committed), the fix was implemented as new enforcement inside the git workflow: a generated_pdfs() function in skills/git/scripts/commit_classifier.py, a new exit-10 commit gate and session-commit pre-flight check in skills/git/scripts/ies-git, and a new Never-stage rule in skills/git/SKILL.md. David corrected the approach: the cleanup workflow should handle generated PDFs; do not create duplication in the git workflow. The git skill's job is to commit what the cleanup pass has already decided is keep-worthy, not to re-implement content-lifecycle rules the cleanup workflow owns.
correction: Revert the git-workflow additions (classifier function, wrapper gates, SKILL.md rule). Implement the generated-PDF rule once, in the shutdown cleanup workflow's purge step: a PDF with a matching markdown source in the same directory is a render artifact and is deleted during cleanup before staging, so it never reaches a commit.
systemic_fix: Applied 2026-10-24: reverted all git-skill/wrapper/classifier additions; added the generated-PDF rule (PDF + same-named .md sibling in the same directory, excluding deliverable folders) to the shutdown cleanup workflow's purge step. err-20261024T164928-M4FT4E's systemic_fix description is superseded by this entry.
